scenes.tts: A cell that can grip still needs to change shape. Shape is the work of actin filaments. Three small G T Pases of the Rho family decide what the filaments build. They work as Ras does. Bound to G T P, each one is on. Bound to G D P, it is off. G E Fs and G A Ps set the balance.
scenes.caption: A cell that can grip still needs to change shape. Shape is the work of actin filaments. Three small GTPases of the Rho family decide what the filaments build. They work as Ras does. Bound to GTP, each one is on. Bound to GDP, it is off. GEFs and GAPs set the balance.
scenes.visual: A cell with faint actin filaments. Three switch chips, Rho, Rac and Cdc42, appear beside it, each with a toggle that turns on with GTP and off with GDP; GEFs and GAPs set the balance.
scenes.narration: A cell that can grip still needs to change shape. Shape is the work of actin filaments. Three small GTPases of the Rho family decide what the filaments build. They work as Ras does. Bound to GTP, each one is on. Bound to GDP, it is off. GEFs and GAPs set the balance.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-two, Anne Ridley and Alan Hall injected purified proteins into fibroblasts. The cells had been starved of serum, which leaves them with little organised actin. Active Rho filled the cells with thick actin cables. Active Rac made their edges ruffle.
scenes.caption: In 1992, Anne Ridley and Alan Hall injected purified proteins into fibroblasts. The cells had been starved of serum, which leaves them with little organised actin. Active Rho filled the cells with thick actin cables. Active Rac made their edges ruffle.
scenes.visual: A starved fibroblast with sparse actin gets a pipette of purified protein. Active Rho fills it with thick cables; the cell resets and active Rac makes its edge ruffle.
scenes.narration: In 1992, Anne Ridley and Alan Hall injected purified proteins into fibroblasts. The cells had been starved of serum, which leaves them with little organised actin. Active Rho filled the cells with thick actin cables. Active Rac made their edges ruffle.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-five, Catherine Nobes and Alan Hall showed that C D C forty-two produces thin spikes. Separately, the laboratory of Louis Lim showed the same. So three switches gave three different shapes.
scenes.caption: In 1995, Catherine Nobes and Alan Hall showed that Cdc42 produces thin spikes. Separately, the laboratory of Louis Lim showed the same. So three switches gave three different shapes.
scenes.visual: The cell resets. Nobes and Hall, then separately Lim's laboratory, point to Cdc42, which grows thin spikes. The three results line up as three cells.
scenes.narration: In 1995, Catherine Nobes and Alan Hall showed that Cdc42 produces thin spikes. Separately, the laboratory of Louis Lim showed the same. So three switches gave three different shapes.

scenes.tts: Rho builds stress fibres. These are cables of actin and myosin two that contract. Rac builds lamellipodia. These are broad, thin sheets, pushed forward by a branching mesh of filaments. C D C forty-two builds filopodia. These are thin fingers with a core of parallel filaments. Keep this rule: each Rho family switch decides which shape the filaments build.
